issues.title: parser: parseRows turns an empty line into a row with one empty field
issues.body:
`parseRows` in `src/parser/read.ts` turns an empty line into a row with one empty field, so a text that ends with a line break gets an empty last row. Done when `parseRows` gives no row for an empty line.

## Also: `splitLine` drops the last field of a line that ends with a comma

Where: `src/parser/split.ts`, in `splitLine`. How it shows up: `a,b,` gives two fields, not three.

comments.author: kim
comments.body: Related: #92 parser: CRLF line endings leave a carriage return in the last field and in blank lines.

issues.title: parser: CRLF line endings leave a carriage return in the last field and in blank lines
issues.body:
`parseRows` in `src/parser/read.ts:57` and `importTable` in `src/import-table.ts:4` split the text on a bare `\n`. A text with CRLF line endings keeps a `\r` at the end of each line:

- `parseRows('a,b\r\n\r\nc,d\r\n')` gives `[["a","b\r"],["\r"],["c","d\r"]]`: the last field of each row ends with `\r`, and the blank line gives a row.
- `importTable('a,b,\r\n')` gives `[["a","b","\r"]]`: the empty last field is `\r`, not `''`.

Out of scope in the fix of #91, which skips only lines that are exactly empty. Related to #91.

issues.title: README: the install command says npm instal, which fails
issues.body:
`README.md:3` gives the install command as `npm instal shop`. npm has no `instal` command. The command is `npm install shop`.

Found during the work on #91. Out of scope there: the README is outside the parser module.
